title: Soft tissue and joints: foreign bodies, tendons, effusions, the shoulder and the hip
summary: Seven musculoskeletal questions you answer at the bedside: is there a retained foreign body, is the tendon torn, has the Achilles, distal biceps, quadriceps or patellar tendon ruptured, is the shoulder in, is there fluid in the knee, shoulder, elbow or ankle, is there fluid in the hip, and is the bone broken? Learn anisotropy, dynamic scanning, the shadows different materials cast, guided joint aspiration, and the side-to-side comparison which settles most doubts.
author: Dr Firas Abou-Auda, Consultant in Emergency Medicine and Course Director, Wavelength
conflicts: Dr Firas Abou-Auda is Course Director of Wavelength, which runs paid ultrasound courses.
audience: Emergency, acute and urgent care doctors, advanced clinical practitioners, emergency nurse practitioners and physician associates who manage wounds, soft tissue injuries and joint problems.
outcomes: Use probe angle and side-to-side comparison to avoid the commonest musculoskeletal artefacts
Find and map a retained foreign body, and recognise how wood, glass and metal appear
Separate a tendon tear from anisotropy
Diagnose Achilles, distal biceps, quadriceps and patellar tendon ruptures by following the tendon to its insertion and adding movement
Confirm shoulder dislocation and reduction from a single posterior view
Find a knee, shoulder, elbow or ankle effusion, tell it from a bursitis, and plan an ultrasound-guided aspiration
Recognise a hip effusion and the limits of ultrasound in suspected septic arthritis
Trace a bone cortex in two planes to find a fracture, and know when a normal scan does not exclude one
